narr: A low pressure system brought a warm front and then cold front into West Virginia on May 28th. The cold front became stationary and then weakened over the area later that night. While rainfall amounts for the 28th were mainly less than an inch and a half, a couple of inches fell over localized portions of Harrison and Taylor Counties. Rainfall from the previous day had also helped to saturate the ground, making flooding easier to occur. In Harrison and Taylor Counties, several roadways flooded and at least one water rescue occurred in the midst of the heavy rain.
ev: Flooding was observed on and around Good Hope Pike from Sunny Croft Country Club to Davisson Run Road and Milford Street.
Flooding was observed along Benedum Drive and along streets and creeks from Bridgeport east to the Taylor County line and north to the Marion County line.
A water rescue occurred on Milford Street in Clarksburg. Flooding was also observed in Nutter Fort and along Elk Avenue in Stonewood.
In downtown Clarksburg, Grant Street was flooded.
Philippi Pike Road in Anmoore was flooded for a period of time.
